chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from one of our companions who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the people take their places in Mina, a Caller calls out: O Mina! Your people have come. Therefore expand your glens and irrigate your resorts! And a Caller calls out: Had you known the One you are being welcomed by, you would have been convinced with the replacement after the Forgiveness.'

key_terms.الْخَلَفُ: Recompense or replacement, referring to the reward for expenditure or effort
key_terms.فِجَاجُ: Glens or valleys, referring to the expanses of Mina
key_terms.مَثَابُ: Resorts or places of return, referring to the dwellings or resting places
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a holy site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Mina during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith highlights the metaphysical presence of Mina as a receptive entity, personified to welcome the pilgrims, reflecting the concept of *alam al-mithal* (the world of images) where physical spaces hold spiritual agency. The second caller’s exclamation underscores the epistemic gap between the pilgrim and the Divine Presence, suggesting that true certainty (*yaqin*) in the status of the One being welcomed would guarantee immediate forgiveness and recompense. This narrative serves as a reminder that Hajj is not merely a physical journey but a spiritual encounter with the Divine Reality, where awareness transforms ritual into salvation.
